messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] different ways of extracting inlabru spatial parameters
parts:
Hi,

I'm not sure what the size of your domain is, or what settings you used for the prior, but some general comments:
the summary.hyperpar output should be more accurate than the values computed from the marginals (as there is some information loss in the storage of those compared with INLAs internal calculations).
The "base model" in the PC-prior is a model with "infinite range and zero variance", i.e. in a model with a purely linear spatial effect of the locations (a plane), it would penalise deviation from that plane.
(The other extreme would be correlation range zero, but that is tricky in continuous space as the limiting behaviour is independent for each location; this is fine for a finite set of locations but it doesn't give a very interpretable continuous domain field.)

So if you weren't expecting spatial correlation (as you sai in your follow up) you need to consider the amplitude of the effect, not just the range. It looks like the variance (or std.dev. sigma) is quite small, which means the spatial component has little influence on the predictor (unless the scale of the data is also very small; that depends on the details of your problem...)

Finn
